source.title: Open problems in commutative ring theory

accepted.question_text: For a Prüfer ring R, is the finitistic projective dimension fp.dim R always at most 1?

evidence.quote: Problem 1a. Let R be a Prüfer ring. Is fp.dim R ≤ 1?

accepted.question_text: For a total ring of quotients R, is the finitistic projective dimension fp.dim R always equal to 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 1b. Let R be a total ring of quotients. Is fp.dim R = 0?

accepted.question_text: If R is a Gaussian ring, must its weak global dimension w.dim R be 0, 1, or infinite?
accepted.context_brief: Gaussian rings and weak global dimension

evidence.quote: Problem 2a. If R is a Gaussian ring, then is w.dim R = 0, 1, or ∞?

accepted.question_text: If R is a total ring of quotients, must its weak global dimension w.dim R be 0, 1, or infinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 2b. If R is a total ring of quotients, is w.dim R = 0, 1, or ∞?

accepted.question_text: What values can the weak global dimension w.dim R take when R is a Prüfer ring?
accepted.context_brief: Prüfer rings and weak global dimension

evidence.quote: Problem 2c. What are the values of w.dim R when R is a Prüfer ring?

accepted.question_text: If D is a one-dimensional coherent domain, is the integral closure of D inside its field of quotients always a Prüfer domain?

evidence.quote: Is the integral closure of a one dimensional coherent domain in its field of quotients a Prüfer domain?

accepted.question_text: Assume that R is a G-GCD ring and G is a finitely generated abelian group. Do the finite conductor property and the quasi coherent property both ascend from R to the group ring RG?
accepted.context_brief: Group rings and ascent of properties

evidence.quote: Problem 4a. Assume that R is a G-GCD ring and G is a finitely generated abelian group. Do the finite conductor and the quasi coherent properties ascend from R to RG?

accepted.question_text: Are the finite conductor property and the quasi coherent property genuinely different properties for commutative rings, or do they coincide?

evidence.quote: Problem 4b. Are the finite conductor and quasi coherent properties for rings distinct?

accepted.question_text: For a commutative ring R and an abelian group G whose element orders are invertible in R, is there a formula for the global dimension of RG in terms of the global dimension of R together with some invariant of G, analogous to the known formula for weak global dimension?

evidence.quote: Problem 5a. Is there a similar formula that relates the global dimension of RG to the global dimension of R in combination with some invariant of the group G?

accepted.question_text: Find characterizations of commutative group rings that are semisimple and of commutative group rings that are hereditary.

evidence.quote: Problem 5b. Find characterizations of semisimple and hereditary group rings.

accepted.question_text: Determine when a commutative group ring RG, with R a commutative ring and G an abelian group, is Cohen–Macaulay or Gorenstein in the non-Noetherian sense introduced in the cited literature.
accepted.context_brief: Non-Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay and Gorenstein group rings

evidence.quote: The questions of when a group ring RG, where R is a commutative ring and G is an abelian group, is Cohen-Macaulay or Gorenstein have yet to be investigated.

accepted.question_text: Find a non-Noetherian characterization of local complete intersection rings that is compatible with the coherent setting in the sense that coherent local Gorenstein rings are complete intersections and coherent local complete intersection rings are Cohen–Macaulay.

evidence.quote: Is there a non-Noetherian characterization of local complete intersection rings such that (coherent) local Gorenstein rings are complete intersections, and such that (coherent) local complete intersection rings are Cohen-Macaulay?

accepted.question_text: Is every weakly quasi-complete Noetherian local ring quasi-complete?

evidence.quote: Problem 8a. Is a weakly quasi-complete ring quasi-complete?

accepted.question_text: Let k be a field and let R = k[X1, …, Xn] localized at the maximal ideal (X1, …, Xn) with n ≥ 2. Is R weakly quasi-complete, and in particular is it quasi-complete?

evidence.quote: Problem 8b. Let k be a field and R = k[X1; : : : ; Xn](X1;:::;Xn), n ≥ 2. Is R (weakly) quasi-complete?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an integrally closed reduced ring R such that for every maximal ideal M the localization RM is an integrally closed McCoy ring, while R itself is not a McCoy ring and is not locally a domain?

evidence.quote: Does there exist an integrally closed reduced ring R such that RM is an integrally closed McCoy ring for each maximal ideal M, but R is not a McCoy ring and it is not locally a domain?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist reduced rings that satisfy both property (a.c.) and property (An) for some n ≥ 2, but are nevertheless not McCoy rings?

evidence.quote: Do there exist reduced rings that have both (a.c.) and (An) for some n ≥ 2 that are not McCoy rings?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a nonzero prime ideal of a Prüfer domain R. Characterize those pairs (P, R) such that for every Prüfer domain T contained in R with the same quotient field, the contracted prime P ∩ T is a divisorial prime ideal of T.

evidence.quote: Problem 11a. Characterize when P (and R) is such that P∩T is a divisorial prime of T for each Prüfer domain T ⊆ R with the same quotient field as R.

accepted.question_text: Let P be a nonzero prime ideal of a Prüfer domain R. Characterize those pairs (P, R) such that there is no Prüfer domain T contained in R with the same quotient field for which P ∩ T becomes a divisorial prime of T.

evidence.quote: Problem 11b. Characterize when P (and R) is such that there is no Prüfer domain T ⊆ R with the same quotient field as R such that P ∩ T is a divisorial prime of T.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime ideal P and a countably infinite ascending chain of overrings R = R0 ⊂ R1 ⊂ R2 ⊂ ··· ⊂ RP such that PR2n is divisorial in R2n and PR2n+1 is not divisorial in R2n+1 for every n ≥ 0; and if such a chain exists, is PS divisorial or not divisorial in the union S = ⋃ Rm?

evidence.quote: Problem 12a. Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime P such that there is a countably infinite chain of overrings ... where for all n ≥ 0, PR2n is a divisorial ideal of R2n and PR2n+1 is an ideal of R2n+1 that is not divisorial? If such a chain exists, is PS divisorial or not divisorial as an ideal of S = ⋃Rm (⊆ RP)?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime ideal P and a countably infinite descending chain of underrings R = R0 ⊋ R1 ⊋ R2 ⊋ ··· ⊋ T with the same quotient field such that P ∩ R2n is divisorial in R2n and P ∩ R2n+1 is not divisorial in R2n+1 for every n ≥ 0; and if such a chain exists, is P ∩ T divisorial or not divisorial in T?

evidence.quote: Problem 12b. Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime P such that there is a countably infinite chain of underrings ... where for all n ≥ 0, P ∩ R2n is a divisorial ideal of R2n and P ∩ R2n+1 is not a divisorial ideal of R2n+1? If such a chain exists, is P ∩ T divisorial or not divisorial as an ideal of T?

accepted.question_text: If RP and R/P are straight domains, must the pullback ring R + P RP also be a straight domain?

evidence.quote: Problem 13a. If RP and R/P are straight domains does this imply that R + P RP is a straight domain?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a straight domain that is not locally divided?
accepted.context_brief: Straight domains vs locally divided domains

evidence.quote: Problem 13b. Does there exist a straight domain which is not locally divided?

accepted.question_text: For an integral domain D, is the Krull dimension of the ring Int(D) of integer-valued polynomials always bounded above by the Krull dimension of D[X], equivalently does dim(Int(D)) ≤ dim(D[X]) always hold?

evidence.quote: The question of an upper bound remains open: It is conjectured to be equal to dim(D[X]).

accepted.question_text: Let D be a one-dimensional local Noetherian domain with finite residue field. Give necessary and sufficient conditions for Int(D) to satisfy the almost strong Skolem property.

evidence.quote: Considering a one-dimensional local Noetherian domain D with finite residue field, when does Int(D) satisfy the almost strong Skolem property?

accepted.question_text: Besides the known examples coming from iterates of nonconstant integer polynomials and affine transformations of the three displayed examples in the paper, are there any other natural self-ordered sequences of integers?

evidence.quote: Are there any other 'natural' self ordered sequences neither obtained by a dynamical construction nor by an affine map applied to the three previous examples?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist subsets E of the integers such that the associated sequence of Bhargava factorials {n!E} is not ultimately strictly increasing?

evidence.quote: Are there subsets E of Z such that the sequence of Bhargava’s factorials {n!E} is not ultimately strictly increasing?

accepted.question_text: For which infinite subsets E of the integers is the constant eE obtained from the Bhargava-factorial construction transcendental?
accepted.context_brief: Transcendence of constants from abstract factorials

evidence.quote: For which infinite subset E is eE a transcendental number?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary integral domain D, is the ring Int(D) of integer-valued polynomials always flat as a D-module?

evidence.quote: Problem 19a. Is Int(D) a flat D-module for any domain D?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary integral domain D, is the ring Int(D) of integer-valued polynomials always free as a D-module?

evidence.quote: Problem 19b. Is Int(D) a free D-module for any domain D?

accepted.question_text: For an integral domain D and any positive integer n, is the canonical D-algebra homomorphism Int(D)⊗D n → Int(Dn) always injective, always surjective, or always an isomorphism?
accepted.context_brief: Tensor products and multivariable integer-valued polynomials

evidence.quote: Is this canonical morphism always injective? surjective?

accepted.question_text: For an integral domain D, does Int(D) always admit a unique D–D-biring structure for which the inclusion D[X] → Int(D) is a homomorphism of D–D-birings?

evidence.quote: Let D be an integral domain. Does Int(D) always have a unique structure of a D-D-biring such that the inclusion D[X] → Int(D) is a homomorphism of D-D-birings?

accepted.question_text: Let D ⊆ A be an extension of domains. If Int(D) ⊆ Int(A), must the extension D ⊆ A be almost polynomially complete, meaning that Int(Dn) ⊆ Int(An) for every positive integer n?

evidence.quote: If Int(D) ⊆ Int(A), does it follow that the extension D ⊆ A is almost polynomially complete?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a number field with ring of integers OK. Prove or disprove that the natural density δ(Int(OK)) of the non-negative integers n for which Intn(OK) is a free OK-module exists, is rational, and is at least 1 divided by the cardinality of the Pólya group of OK; then compute that density.

evidence.quote: Prove or disprove the following conjecture: δ(Int(OK)) exists, is rational, and is at least 1/Card(PO(OK)). Then compute δ(Int(OK)).

accepted.question_text: Let E be the set of values of a second-order recursive integer sequence un+1 = a un + b un−1 with initial values u0 and u1. Compute a regular basis, meaning a basis whose nth term has degree n, for the Z-module Int(E; Z).

evidence.quote: Problem 24a. Compute a regular basis (that is, a basis with n-th term of degree n) of the Z-module Int(E; Z).

accepted.question_text: For the same recursive set E, compute for each prime p the characteristic sequence of Int(E; Z), namely the sequence αp(n) given by the p-adic valuation of the fractional ideal of leading coefficients of elements of Int(E; Z) of degree at most n.

evidence.quote: Problem 24b. Compute the characteristic sequence of Int(E; Z) with respect to each prime p.

accepted.question_text: For the same recursive set E, determine the asymptotic behavior of the characteristic sequence, in particular compute the limit of α(n)/n as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem 24c. Determine the asymptotic behavior of this sequence, that is, compute the limit lim n→∞ α(n)/n.

accepted.question_text: Compute a regular basis of the ring IntQ(Mn(Z)) of rational-coefficient polynomials that are integer-valued on n×n integer matrices.

evidence.quote: Problem 25a. Compute a regular basis of IntQ(Mn(Z)).

accepted.question_text: Compute the characteristic sequence of IntQ(Mn(Z)) with respect to each prime p.

evidence.quote: Problem 25b. Compute its characteristic sequence with respect to each prime p.

accepted.question_text: Determine the asymptotic behavior of the characteristic sequence for IntQ(Mn(Z)).

evidence.quote: Problem 25c. Determine the asymptotic behavior of this sequence.

accepted.question_text: Let D be an integral domain with quotient field K, and let A be a torsion-free D-algebra that is finitely generated as a D-module. Determine for which such algebras A the inclusion ⋂a∈A (D[X] + μa(X)K[X]) ⊆ IntK(A) is actually an equality.

evidence.quote: For which algebras A as above does this inclusion become an equality?

accepted.question_text: Give an example of a D-algebra A for which Int(A) is not a ring, possibly after relaxing some of the standing hypotheses such as finite generation as a D-module.
accepted.context_brief: When Int(A) fails to be a ring

evidence.quote: Problem 27a. Give an example of a D-algebra A such that Int(A) is not a ring.

accepted.question_text: When D has finite residue rings, prove the conjecture that Int(A) is always a ring for every torsion-free D-algebra A of the type described in the paper, or produce a counterexample.

evidence.quote: Problem 27b. It is conjectured that Int(A) is always a ring when D has finite residue rings. Prove this conjecture or give a counterexample in this case.

accepted.question_text: Determine when the integral closure of IntK(A) is a Prüfer domain.

evidence.quote: Determine when this integral closure is Prüfer.

accepted.question_text: Describe the integrally closed rings that lie between a two-dimensional Noetherian domain and its quotient field.

evidence.quote: Describe the integrally closed rings between a two-dimensional Noetherian domain and its quotient field.

accepted.question_text: If I is an n-absorbing ideal of a commutative ring R, must I also be strongly n-absorbing?

evidence.quote: Problem 30a. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is I a strongly n-absorbing ideal of R?

accepted.question_text: If I is an n-absorbing ideal of a commutative ring R, must rad(I)^n be contained in I?

evidence.quote: Problem 30b. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is rad(I)^n ⊆ I?

accepted.question_text: If I is an n-absorbing ideal of a commutative ring R, is the extended ideal I[X] necessarily n-absorbing in the polynomial ring R[X]?

evidence.quote: Problem 30c. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is I[X] an n-absorbing ideal of the polynomial ring R[X]?

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of projective star operations for projective varieties, equivalently for finitely generated field extensions F/K that need not be purely transcendental.

evidence.quote: Develop projective star operations for projective varieties.

accepted.question_text: Is every stable Archimedean domain one-dimensional?

evidence.quote: Problem 32a. Is a stable Archimedean domain one-dimensional?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a one-dimensional Mori domain in which every divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Does it follow that every divisorial ideal of D is stable?

evidence.quote: Problem 32b. Let D be a one-dimensional Mori domain such that each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Is it true that each divisorial ideal is stable?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a Mori domain in which every divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Does it follow that D is v-stable?

evidence.quote: Problem 32c. Let D be a Mori domain such that each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Is it true that D is v-stable?

accepted.question_text: Assume that D is a finitely stable LPI-domain. Must D have finite character?
accepted.context_brief: Finite character of finitely stable LPI-domains

evidence.quote: Assume that D is a finitely stable LPI-domain. Is it true that D has finite character?

accepted.question_text: Let D be an integral domain, S a multiplicatively closed subset of D, DS the localization, and R = D + XDS[X]. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for R to be a v-domain; in particular, prove or disprove that this holds exactly when D is a v-domain and each ideal (d, X) with nonzero d in D is v-invertible.
accepted.context_brief: v-domains of the form D + XDS[X]

evidence.quote: Problem 34a. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for R = D + XDS[X] to be a v-domain. Prove or disprove that R is a v-domain if and only if D is a v-domain and (d, X) is v-invertible for all d ≠ 0.

accepted.question_text: More generally, for an extension of integral domains A ⊆ B, find necessary and sufficient conditions for the domain A + XB[X] to be a v-domain.

evidence.quote: Problem 34b. Let A ⊆ B be an extension of integral domains, and let X be an indeterminate over B. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the integral domain A + XB[X] to be a v-domain.

accepted.question_text: Let D be an almost GCD domain such that every nonzero t-locally principal ideal is t-invertible. Must D have finite t-character?
accepted.context_brief: Almost GCD domains and finite t-character

evidence.quote: Let D be an almost GCD domain such that every nonzero t-locally principal ideal is t-invertible. Is D of finite t-character?

accepted.question_text: Let T be a non-empty collection of overrings of an integral domain D, and for each T in that collection let ?T be a semistar operation on T. Find conditions on the family of overrings and the semistar operations ensuring that the induced semistar operation E ↦ ⋂(ET)?T on D is of finite type.

evidence.quote: Problem 36a. Find conditions on T and on the semistar operations ?T under which the semistar operation ?T on D ... is of finite type.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a non-empty collection of semistar operations on an integral domain D, and define the intersection semistar operation ÊS by EÊS = ⋂ E? for ? in S. Find conditions on S ensuring that ÊS is of finite type.

evidence.quote: Problem 36b. Let S be any non-empty collection of semistar operations on D ... Find conditions on the set S for the semistar operation ÊS on D to be of finite type.

accepted.question_text: Is there a Krull domain, or even a factorial domain, D such that the polynomial ring D[X] has dimension strictly larger than 1 + dim(D)?

evidence.quote: Problem 37a. Is there a Krull (or, more particularly, factorial) domain D such that 1 + dim(D) < dim(D[X])?

accepted.question_text: For David’s ascending-union example J = ⋃ Jn of a 3-dimensional factorial domain, is J locally Jaffard?
accepted.context_brief: Local Jaffard property of David's domain

evidence.quote: Problem 37b. Is J a locally Jaffard domain?

accepted.question_text: Let A ⊆ D be an extension of integral domains where A is Noetherian and D is a subalgebra of an affine A-domain T. Must D be locally Jaffard?
accepted.context_brief: Locally Jaffard subalgebras of affine domains

evidence.quote: Problem 37c. Let A ⊆ D be an extension of integral domains, where A is a Noetherian domain and D is a subalgebra of an affine domain T over A. Is D a locally Jaffard domain?

accepted.question_text: If R is a one-dimensional local Mori domain, must R be locally tame?

evidence.quote: Let R be a one-dimensional local Mori domain. Is R locally tame?

accepted.question_text: Analyze and describe the non-unique factorization behavior of Int(D) when D is a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field.

evidence.quote: Analyze and describe non-unique factorization in Int(D), where D is a DVR with finite residue field.

accepted.question_text: Find axioms that characterize the partially ordered set Spec(Q[x, y]).

evidence.quote: Problem 40a. Find axioms characterizing the poset Q[x, y].

accepted.question_text: Are the prime spectra Spec(Q[x, y]) and Spec(Q(√2)[x, y]) order-isomorphic as partially ordered sets?

evidence.quote: Problem 40b. Are Spec(Q[x, y]) and Spec(Q(√2)[x, y]) order-isomorphic?

accepted.question_text: More generally, if F and K are algebraic number fields and A is a two-dimensional affine domain over F, is Spec(A) order-isomorphic to Spec(K[x, y])?

evidence.quote: Problem 40c. More generally, let F and K be algebraic number fields. If A is a two-dimensional affine domain over F, is Spec(A) order-isomorphic to Spec(K[x, y])?

accepted.question_text: If F and K are fields that are not algebraic over finite fields and Spec(F[x, y]) is order-isomorphic to Spec(K[x, y]), must F and K be isomorphic as fields?

evidence.quote: Problem 40d. If Spec(F[x, y]) and Spec(K[x, y]) are order-isomorphic ... are F and K necessarily isomorphic fields?

accepted.question_text: Let I be the integral closure of the monomial ideal (x^a, y^b, z^c) in a polynomial ring over a field. Classify all triples (a, b, c) for which every power of I is integrally closed.

evidence.quote: Classify all triples (a, b, c) for which all powers of I are integrally closed.

accepted.question_text: Is there a more direct algorithm for computing the integral closure of a general ideal than the standard approach of computing the integral closure of the entire Rees algebra?
accepted.context_brief: Algorithms for integral closure of ideals

evidence.quote: Problem 42a. Is there a more direct algorithm for computing the integral closure of a general ideal?

accepted.question_text: Can the Leonard–Pellikaan and Singh–Swanson algorithms be modified to compute the integral closure of ideals?

evidence.quote: Problem 42b. Can the Leonard–Pellikaan and Singh–Swanson algorithms be modified for computing the integral closure of ideals?

accepted.question_text: Determine how tight the general Lipman–Sathaye theorem stated in the paper is by relaxing one or more assumptions and either proving the resulting statement or producing a counterexample.

evidence.quote: The suggested problem is to find how tight is the statement of this theorem: relax some assumption and either prove the theorem or find a counterexample for that relaxation.

accepted.question_text: Construct a Noetherian two-dimensional complete integrally closed local domain of the Cutkosky type in which every m-primary ideal has more than one Rees valuation.

evidence.quote: Cutkosky proved ... the existence of a Noetherian, two-dimensional, complete, integrally closed local domain (R, m) in which every m-primary ideal has more than one Rees valuation. Give a construction of such a ring.

trace.notes: Mapped a 25-page PDF with one main Open Problems section spanning Problems 1 through 44 and identified explicit subproblems 1a–40d.
Extracted explicit problem statements and named subproblems from pages 3 through 20, preserving page-level citations from the PDF text.

Rewrote each extracted item into a standalone question by inlining local context such as the relevant ring class, construction, or algebraic setting when the source statement depended on nearby sentences.
Kept distinct subproblems separate and did not merge items because the source presents them as different open questions with materially different targets.
Accepted only items with direct page-cited evidence from the readable PDF; no items required escalation to needs_review because each accepted question could be grounded in nearby source text.
Saved the exact JSON payload to outputs/parse-paper/OpenProblemsInCommutativeRingTheory.Springer14.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
